candidates.label: Seleucia Pieria archaeological site
candidates.support: Seleucia Pieria, the seaport of Antioch, about 16 miles from the city and about 5 miles north of the mouth of the Orontes. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on this coastal site; Wikidata's own record places it within Hatay Province, Türkiye.

scripture.textWEB: So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.

candidates.label: Attalia (modern Antalya)
candidates.support: A city on Pamphylia's coast founded by Attalus II Philadelphus, continuously inhabited today as Antalya, Türkiye. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site.

scripture.textWEB: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

candidates.label: Samothrace (island)
candidates.support: An island in the north Aegean Sea, south of Thrace, with a town at its northern end where ships could anchor for the night. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the island, known today as Samothraki.

scripture.textWEB: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;

candidates.label: Amphipolis archaeological site
candidates.support: A town in Macedonia on the river Strymon, on the Via Egnatia. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, which Wikidata places in today's municipality of Amphipolis.

scripture.textWEB: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

candidates.label: Apollonia (Macedonia, on the Via Egnatia)
candidates.support: A town in Mygdonia, Macedonia, on the Via Egnatia between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, about 30 Roman miles from Amphipolis and 38 from Thessalonica. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, near the modern village of Nea Apollonia; the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia reports that its name seems to survive in the modern Pollina.

scripture.textWEB: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

candidates.label: Assos archaeological site
candidates.support: An ancient city of the Troad on a rocky height on the south coast, in the Roman province of Asia. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, known today as Behramkale, an alternate name recorded on the Wikidata item itself.

scripture.textWEB: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.
When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

candidates.label: Mitylene (chief city of Lesbos)
candidates.support: The chief city of the island of Lesbos, with two harbors. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, the modern city of Mytilene, Greece.

scripture.textWEB: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

candidates.label: Chios (island)
candidates.support: An Aegean island south of Lesbos, close to the Asia Minor mainland. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the island, which keeps the name Chios today. The point is the island's principal town, also called Chios.

scripture.textWEB: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

candidates.label: Samos (island)
candidates.support: An Aegean island between Ephesus and Miletus, joined to the Roman province of Asia. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the island, which keeps the name Samos today.

scripture.textWEB: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

candidates.label: Trogyllium (promontory opposite Samos)
candidates.support: A promontory on the Asia Minor coast opposite Samos, extending from the Mycale mountains, with an anchorage. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, which Pleiades identifies as today's Dip Burun. Several early manuscripts omit the clause naming it in Acts 20:15; see the route's note.

scripture.textWEB: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

candidates.label: Cos (island)
candidates.support: An Aegean island off the coast of Caria, one of the six cities of the Dorian Hexapolis. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the island, known today as Kos.

scripture.textWEB: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

candidates.label: Rhodes (city)
candidates.support: The chief city of the island of Rhodes, in the southeastern Aegean. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the city of Rhodes as the site.

scripture.textWEB: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

candidates.label: Patara archaeological site
candidates.support: A coastal city of Lycia with a celebrated oracle of Apollo and a harbor serving trade with the interior. The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia gives Gelemiş as the modern name of the ruin; Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site.

scripture.textWEB: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

candidates.label: Myra archaeological site
candidates.support: A Lycian city with a harbor used by grain ships from Alexandria. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site; Wikidata's own record places it within Demre district, Türkiye.

scripture.textWEB: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

candidates.label: Cnidus (Cape Krio / Tekir site)
candidates.support: A city of Caria at the end of a long, narrow peninsula, with two harbors. Pleiades records that in the late fourth century BC the city's political center moved here, to Tekir, from an older site at Burgaz, so the city Paul's ship passed was at Tekir. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the Tekir site; Wikidata's own record places it within Datça, Muğla Province, Türkiye.

scripture.textWEB: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

candidates.label: Salmone (promontory, Crete)
candidates.support: The promontory forming the northeastern corner of Crete. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, identified with today's Cape Sideros.

scripture.textWEB: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

candidates.label: Fair Havens (Kaloi Limenes)
candidates.support: A roadstead on Crete's south coast about 5 miles east of Cape Matala, sheltered from north and northwest winds but judged unsuitable for wintering. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site; its Greek name, Kaloi Limenes, is a direct translation of 'Fair Havens.'

scripture.textWEB: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

candidates.label: Cauda (island south of Crete)
candidates.support: A small island south of Crete. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, identified with today's Gavdos, whose modern Greek name reflects the 'Cauda' manuscript reading rather than 'Clauda.'

scripture.textWEB: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

candidates.label: Sidon (ancient Phoenician port)
candidates.support: An ancient Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, continuously inhabited today as Sidon, Lebanon.

scripture.textWEB: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

candidates.label: Syracuse (Sicily)
candidates.support: A Greek colony on Sicily's east coast and capital of the Roman province of Sicily. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, known today as Syracuse (Siracusa).

scripture.textWEB: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

candidates.label: Rhegium (Sicilian Strait)
candidates.support: A city on the Italian shore of the Sicilian Strait. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, known today as Reggio Calabria.

scripture.textWEB: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

candidates.label: Three Taverns (Tres Tabernae, Appian Way)
candidates.support: A station on the Appian Way about 33 Roman miles from Rome. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site.

scripture.textWEB: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

stops.name: Forum of Appius
stops.todayName: In the comune of Latina, Italy

candidates.label: Forum of Appius (Forum Appii, Appian Way)
candidates.support: A station on the Appian Way about 43 Roman miles from Rome, where a canal through the Pontine Marshes began. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site; Wikidata's own record places it within the comune of Latina, Italy. None of six popular English versions compared uses the World English Bible's wording, 'The Market of Appius'; three read 'Forum of Appius'. See the route's note.

scripture.textWEB: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

candidates.label: Ptolemais (Phoenician coast)
candidates.support: A Phoenician coastal city, identified with the Old Testament's Acco. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, known today as Acre (Akko).

scripture.textWEB: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.
